summary: Pair of range lights lit 10 October 1889 on the eastern shore of Georgian Bay: a square wooden front tower with keeper's house, and a steel rear tower of 1909; boat access only.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1888 (Wikidata) against LighthouseFriends' 'Erected in 1889' and the first display on 10 October 1889. The Parks Canada heritage statement (search snippet only; the page did not load) gives construction in 1888-89. The story uses 1889, the year the light was first shown.
The 1903 annual report says the steel frame was painted red and the woodwork white. LighthouseFriends says the reverse. The story follows the annual report.

The 1889 Department description gives the front light as fixed white. LighthouseFriends' table and the current Coast Guard list both give fixed red for the front light (and for the rear). Not resolved in the sources: the story reports the 1889 colour and the current colour.

LighthouseFriends' rear-light table gives 'Present tower erected in 1903', but its own text and the 1909 Department report give the four-section steel tower as 1909, replacing the 1903 tower. The story follows the text and the 1909 report.

notes_for_editor: (1) Thin on wrecks and rescues: none found in the sources read, the corpus Marine reports (1900 onward) mention no wreck here, and a Chronicling America search for 'Pointe au Baril' with 'lighthouse' (1889-1930) returned nothing. No Storms chapter is written. (2) Keepers: the roster is LighthouseFriends' list of head keepers, not checked against the Department's keepers' tables in the corpus (not searched for this station). Samuel Edward Oldfield's 1897 dismissal rests on LighthouseFriends alone. (3) Living person: Emmaline Madigan is named only in her public role, as the Township and LighthouseFriends print it (keeper 1977-1983; summer historian and museum curator 2000-2024; retired 2024). No family or personal details are used, per the 'people who may be alive' rule. (4) The Parks Canada federal heritage page (FHBRO 6282) did not load; the 1888-89 construction date is from a search snippet only and is not cited. (5) Current status: the Coast Guard list (read 27 Oct 2026) still gives both range lights as active. LighthouseFriends says they were on the list to be decommissioned, with a township proposal to buy them; the outcome is not found. The 2025 museum notice says the lighthouse was under renovation. (6) Access: LighthouseFriends' seasonal hours and the boat-only access are undated; check with the township. (7) Role 'head keeper' follows LighthouseFriends' 'Head Keepers' list for this station. (8) Fact-check 2026-10-27: the 1903 tower colours, the 1904 slats and trees, and the 1909 replacement were checked against the annual reports' printed pages (p. 49, p. 47, p. 65). No names or dates in this station were matched by column position. (9) The 2025 museum notice says the stored artifacts came from a project with the township while the lighthouse 'undergoes renovations'; it does not say the exhibition showed those artifacts, so the story no longer says so. The notice's name for the museum is 'WPSDMuseum'. (10) The story now states the front light's colour as 1889 white and current red (LighthouseFriends and the Coast Guard list). (11) The access notes (boat only; summer hours) are undated and the story says so.
